summary: This is a JUnit test that checks the thermostat's printStatusToDisplay() method writes the right text to the console. Because the method prints instead of returning a value, the test has to temporarily capture System.out and inspect the captured text.

lines.text: A ByteArrayOutputStream is a bucket in memory that collects bytes instead of sending them to the screen, so anything printed into it can be read back as a String later.
The real console stream is saved first, because the test is about to replace it and has to be able to put it back.
This redirects System.out so every println() inside the method under test lands in the in-memory bucket rather than the console.
The finally block runs whether the method succeeds or throws, which guarantees the console is restored; without it, a failure here would silently swallow the output of every later test.

println() appends a line ending, so the expected text must include System.lineSeparator() to match on any operating system — hard-coding "\n" is a classic cause of tests that pass on one machine and fail on another.
Notice how much machinery one small assertion needed. That awkwardness is a design signal: a method that returns its status is far easier to test than one that only prints it.
